turns.learner: Hello teacher. I want to practise joining sentences, because my writing is not good.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Good idea. Joining short sentences makes your writing smoother.

You may know the word "and". It adds one idea to another idea. Here is an example: "I like tea and I like milk." Two short sentences become one sentence.

Now you try. Join with and:
"I have a cat. I have a dog."

turns.learner: I have a cat. And I have a dog.
turns.tutor:
Yes, you used "and" to add the second idea. Good. One small point: in one joined sentence, there is no full stop before "and".

Now try one more by yourself. "But" shows a contrast, a different idea. Join with but:
"The bus is cheap. It is slow."

turns.learner: The bus is cheap. But it is slow.
turns.tutor:
Yes, "But it is slow" shows the contrast. Good. Again, one small point: a joined sentence has no full stop before "but".

Now one more, by yourself. "Because" gives a reason, the why. Join with because:
"I am happy. It is my birthday."

turns.learner: I am happy. Because it is my birthday.
turns.tutor:
Yes, "Because it is my birthday" gives the reason. Good. Remember the small point: the reason stays in the same sentence, so no full stop before "because".

Now write two sentences about your day. Use two different linking words from today: and, but, or because. Use your own ideas.

turns.learner: I woke up early. But I was tired. Because I slept late.
turns.tutor:
Thank you for your sentences about your day. You used "But" for a contrast and "Because" for a reason.

Let us recap:
"and" adds an idea, "but" shows a contrast, "because" gives a reason.
The linking word joins two ideas inside one sentence.

Tell me the rule in your own words.

turns.learner: And is for more, but is different, because is the reason. You put a full stop and then the word.
turns.tutor:
You are right about the meanings: "and" adds, "but" is different, "because" is the reason.

The last part is not right. Do not put a full stop before the linking word. The word stays inside one sentence.

Right: "I was late because the train was slow."
Wrong: "I was late. Because the train was slow."

Now say the rule again in your own words.
